brief: My balcony is partial shade with moderate moisture, and a cat and a dog live in the household. A west-facing balcony with soft afternoon light filtered through a neighbouring tree. My indoor cat loves to sit among the pots.

retrieved.notes: TOXIC to cats and dogs; Saponin; Contact dermatitis, vomiting, anorexia, depression
TOXIC to cats and dogs; Cycasin; Vomiting, melena, icterus, increased thirst, hemorrhagic gastroenteritis, bruising, coagulopathy, liver damage, liver...

design.site_summary: A west-facing partial shade balcony with moderate moisture and pets present, receiving soft afternoon light filtered through a tree.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme stacks three vertical layers starting with trailing foliage baskets above eye level, moving to mid-height structural shrubs against the back wall, and finishing with a low ground-level grazing tray accessible to the cat along the floor.
design.combination_logic: The combination contrasts the broad, tropical leaves of the money tree with the feathery, fine texture of dill and fennel, creating a rich tapestry of green. The waxy foliage and starry blooms of the honey plant provide subtle seasonal rhythm while the structural shrubs offer year-round green architecture.

zones.placement: on the west-facing railing, receiving soft filtered afternoon light.

plants.why: It trails gracefully over the basket edge in partial shade.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides waxy texture and delicate, sweet-scented flowers that contrast with the upright shrubs below.

maintenance: Water when the top two inches of soil are dry.
Feed monthly with balanced liquid fertilizer in spring.
Prune stray long vines after flowering.

zones.placement: against the back west-facing wall in large containers, sheltered by the overhead balcony structure.

plants.why: Thrives in indirect light and adds height with its braided trunk.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as the structural anchor with large palmate leaves providing a bold canopy backdrop.

plants.why: Brings colorful seasonal blooms in partial shade conditions.
plants.role_in_combination: Introduces vivid seasonal color and upright woody stems that contrast with the indoor tropicals.

maintenance: Water weekly to keep soil moderately moist but not waterlogged.
Feed bi-weekly during summer blooming phase.
Prune hibiscus in early spring to encourage new flower buds.

zones.placement: on the floor near the balcony entrance, safe and fully accessible for the indoor cat.

plants.why: Grows easily in pots and provides a safe, feathery texture for cat interaction.
plants.role_in_combination: Offers a delicate, cloud-like textural contrast right at foot level against the heavier pots.

plants.why: Provides an aromatic and safe ground-level herb interest.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds fine needle-like foliage and a subtle anise scent to enrich the sensory experience at ground level.

maintenance: Water every few days to keep the shallow grazing tray consistently moist.
Sow successive seeds every month to maintain fresh foliage.
Trim back spent stems to encourage bushy new growth.

care_instructions.task: Water all mid-level and hanging containers thoroughly
care_instructions.frequency: twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Inspect plants for common pests like aphids on the dill and hibiscus
Bring tender potted shrubs closer to the wall or wrap containers

care_cautions: Overwatering the hanging Hoya carnosa basket can lead to root rot in the filtered west-facing light.
The grazing tray with dill and fennel may be heavily excavated or chewed by the cat, requiring regular reseeding.
design.pet_safety_note: The ground-level grazing zone is stocked exclusively with pet-safe herbs, and toxic plants are elevated out of reach to ensure the cat and dog remain safe.
